questions.question: If $P(A)=0.35$, what is $P(A^c)$ according to a result from the axioms?
Let $S=\{a,b\}$ with $\mathbb{P}(\varnothing)=0$, $\mathbb{P}(\{a\})=1$, $\mathbb{P}(\{b\})=0$ and $\mathbb{P}(S)=1$. Does $\mathbb{P}$ satisfy the axioms of probability?
options: Yes, all three axioms hold
No, the nonempty event $\{b\}$ must have positive probability
No, only $S$ itself can have probability $1$
No, the two outcomes must have equal probability

questions.question: A fair die is rolled. Let $A=\{1,2\}$ and $B=\{2,3\}$. What is $\mathbb{P}(A\cup B)$?
The Kolmogorov axioms are nonnegativity, $\mathbb{P}(S)=1$, and which third axiom?
options: the complement rule $\mathbb{P}(A^c)=1-\mathbb{P}(A)$ for every event
countable additivity for pairwise disjoint events
multiplicativity of probabilities for independent events
additivity $\mathbb{P}(A\cup B)=\mathbb{P}(A)+\mathbb{P}(B)$ for all events

questions.question: Given $\mathbb{P}(\varnothing)=0$, how does countable additivity give $\mathbb{P}(A_1\cup\cdots\cup A_n)=\mathbb{P}(A_1)+\cdots+\mathbb{P}(A_n)$ for pairwise disjoint $A_1,\ldots,A_n$?
options: Drop the disjointness requirement and add all probabilities
Append copies of $S$ to make the finite family a sequence
Append empty events to make the finite family a sequence
Replace the events by independent events with the same probabilities

questions.question: Which argument derives $\mathbb{P}(\varnothing)=0$ from the three axioms without first using finite additivity?
options: $\varnothing$ has no outcomes, so counting gives $\mathbb{P}(\varnothing)=0/|S|=0$
$\mathbb{P}(\varnothing)=0$ is itself one of the three axioms
Countable additivity on $S,\varnothing,\varnothing,\ldots$ plus nonnegativity
Disjointness gives $\mathbb{P}(S\cap\varnothing)=\mathbb{P}(S)\,\mathbb{P}(\varnothing)$

questions.question: Suppose $A\subseteq B$, $\mathbb{P}(A)=0.7$ and $\mathbb{P}(B)=0.6$. What can you conclude?
options: The assignment is valid because both values are nonnegative
The assignment violates monotonicity
$A$ and $B$ must be disjoint
$\mathbb{P}(S)=0.1$
